officialReview.note: All 223 official pairs (CRLF input and output, single line) and both samples parse within 1<=n,m<=10^18 and match the oracle, the isqrt closed form, and (answers<=200000) the literal simulation. No malformed upstream pair or contradiction. 98 official tests have m>=n.

oracle: If m>=n answer n; else binary search the least k in [1,2*10^9] with k(k+1)/2>=n-m and answer m+k (exact Python integers; max answer 1414213563 for n=10^18,m=1). Editorial in the pinned row describes the same reduction.
parse: Exactly one line "n m": two tokens matching [1-9][0-9]* separated by a single space, 1<=n,m<=10^18; LF or CRLF with an optional single final terminator. Rejects signs, underscores, leading zeros, tabs, padding, extra/missing tokens, split lines and blank trailing lines.

authorObservationsNonBinding: 207785393 (WA, passed 15): math.sqrt double formula ceil((-1+sqrt(1+8(n-m)))/2)+m; rounding is wrong near triangular thresholds for large n-m. Python model passes official tests 1..15 and first fails test 16 (999999998765257152 10). 20 extras kill it.

212028901 (WA, passed 3): prints m+1 when m>=n (expected n); model first fails test 4 (1024 1024). Its m<n branch is a day-by-day simulation (TLE risk) that the author did not model beyond correctness.
212034643 (WA, passed 2): prints m+1 when m>=n and uses an approximate sqrt(2n)-2 day count with a two-way final adjustment; model first fails test 3 (32 5 -> prints 13, expected 12).
212025874 (TLE, passed 5): literal simulation, correct but O(answer) days; TLE-only, not an algorithmic counterexample.

212027059 (TLE, passed 5): skips to day m then simulates; besides being slow it is wrong for n<m (returns m instead of n, e.g. 1 2 -> 2), but its recorded verdict is TLE on test 5 (58044 52909, m<n). Parent auditor must judge.
All 12 OK sources read as the same m>=n -> n / least k with k(k+1)/2>=n-m reduction (binary search or sqrt with correction).

semantics: Single line "n m" with 1<=n,m<=10^18 (public English statement shows 10<sup>18</sup>; pinned row flattened it to 1018 and official tests use 1000000000000000000). Barn of capacity n starts full; on day i, m grains are added (capped at n), then i sparrows each eat one grain if any remain. Unique integer: first day at whose end the barn is empty. If m>=n the barn is full every morning and day n empties it, so the answer is n; otherwise the barn stays full through day m and afterwards loses (i-m) net per day, so the answer is m+k for the least k with k(k+1)/2>=n-m. Literal day-by-day simulation exhaustively cross-checks small n,m; an integer-isqrt closed form cross-checks large cases.
